title: Power-law and log-periodic degree tails for a family of probability generating function equations arising in evolving networks
summary: For a fixed integer $j\ge1$ and $0<p<1$, we study the probability generating function (pgf) equation \[ (1+2p)\,g(x)=2p\,x^{j}+g\bigl(x-px+px^{2}\bigr),\qquad 0\le x\le1 , \] which governs the limiting degree distribution $\{p_k\}$ of a family of evolving network models. The cases $j=1$ and $j=2$ are the treelike fast-growth model of Feng and Hu and the homogeneous evolving network of Feng, Li and Hu. We prove that for every $j$ the equation has a unique pgf solution, of mean $2j$, and we determine its coefficient tail exactly: \[ p_k=k^{-1-ρ}\,Ψ_j(\log_λk)+o\bigl(k^{-1-ρ}\bigr), \] where…
